name: railway_a
prompt:
Two images are attached. The first is a layout: 9 outlines on a flat magenta background, in a 3 by 3 grid, all at one shared scale. The first four are strips of railway track; the other five are small pieces of level-crossing equipment. The second image shows finished vehicles from the same game, in the art style to match. Copy its style only, not its vehicles or colours.

Make one image with exactly the same layout as the first image: the same 9 outlines in the same places at the same sizes. Inside each outline, draw what is described for that cell below, as strictly top-down art for a 2D city game.

Shape comes first:
- Fill each outline edge to edge, horizontal, the same size. Draw nothing outside the outlines.
- Inside an outline there is no magenta at all.
- Each track strip (cells 1 to 4) is a piece of an endless straight track, cut square at its left and right ends so it continues seamlessly into a copy of itself placed beside it: the ballast, the rails and the sleepers run right up to the left and right ends with no border, frame or end there. The two thin grey lines across each track outline are exactly where its two rails run, the whole length; paint each rail over its line. The sleepers lie across the strip, square to the rails, evenly spaced along the whole length, and reach about a third of the strip's width past each rail.

Rules for everything:
- Strictly top-down: the camera looks straight down from high above (orthographic plan view, like a map). No side faces, no perspective, no three-quarter view, no tilt, no cast shadow. Flat light from directly above.
- Style: match the style image. Chunky pixel art with crisp hard-edged pixels and no blur. Flat colour with one highlight and one shadow tone. The small equipment (cells 5 to 9) has a dark near-black outline about 2 pixels thick; the track strips have no outline.
- No text, logos, numbers, people or watermark anywhere.
- Outside the outlines, keep the background flat pure magenta #FF00FF. No grid lines or frames.

Cells, row by row, left to right, length x width:
1. 7.2 x 4.4 m - mainline railway track: grey crushed-granite ballast filling the whole strip edge to edge, a little darker at the long edges; 12 evenly spaced pale grey concrete sleepers across it; two steel rails along the grey lines, each a bright polished running strip with a darker rusty-brown edge either side; light rust stains between the rails
2. 7.2 x 4.4 m - mainline railway track: blue-grey crushed-stone ballast filling the strip edge to edge; 12 evenly spaced light concrete sleepers with dark rail fastening clips where the rails cross them; two steel rails along the grey lines, bright worn running strips with dark brown edges
3. 7.2 x 4.4 m - railway track: brownish-grey ballast filling the strip edge to edge; 12 evenly spaced dark brown creosoted timber sleepers, wood grain showing; two steel rails along the grey lines, bright running strips with dark rusty edges
4. 7.2 x 4.4 m - old railway track: weathered grey ballast filling the strip edge to edge, a few tufts of grass along the long edges; 12 evenly spaced worn concrete sleepers, a few chipped; two steel rails along the grey lines, bright running strips with heavy rust either side
5. 4 x 0.3 m - a level-crossing barrier arm lying flat: a long thin boom in bold alternating red and white bands, a small dark hub at its left (pivot) end, two small round red lamps on top, unlit (dark red glass, no glow), its tip at the right
6. 4 x 0.3 m - a level-crossing barrier arm lying flat: a long thin aluminium boom with red reflective bands on white, a dark steel clamp at its left (pivot) end, a rubber-capped tip at the right
7. 0.9 x 0.9 m - a level-crossing warning signal from straight above: the round top of a grey post in the middle; across it, running top to bottom, the top edge of a black backboard with two round lamp hoods, one near the top and one near the bottom, each a black half-ring open toward the right with dark unlit red glass inside, no glow
8. 0.9 x 0.6 m - a level-crossing barrier machine from straight above: a compact housing painted yellow and grey with a rounded lid and vents, the barrier's pivot hub at its right end, a short dark counterweight at its left end
9. 1.2 x 0.7 m - a lineside railway relay cabinet from straight above: a grey-green steel roof with a slight ridge along its length, a rain lip round its edge, a small vent on top, a pale concrete plinth showing as a thin rim round it
